messages:
Irina K.: Heads up — after the org-wide RBAC cleanup this morning we got a big spike in 'privilege_escalation' SIEM alerts. Anyone else seeing this?
Jonah M.: Yep, saw ~2.2k alerts clustered around 10:02 UTC. Looks like the role rebindings fired at once.
Carmen L.: I can confirm — `infra-service` bindings were updated by the change script. Audit shows a single change_id for many principals.
Sam R.: Also correlating a bunch of `kms:Decrypt` failures tied to the same period. Could be service accounts losing temporary grants during the rotation.
Irina K.: I put a 30m suppression window on the privilege_escalation rule to avoid alert fatigue. If it doesn't drop off we escalate. :warning:
Jonah M.: Good call. Can we group alerts by `principal` + `change_id` and dedupe for 10m? That should collapse the storm without hiding unique anomalies.
Carmen L.: Agreed. Proposed quick rule change: add `group_by: [principal, change_id]` and `max_per_group: 1` with a 10m window. Also add a low-severity tag when change_id matches known rollout IDs.
sec-bot: Detected correlated events: count=2178, top_principals=[infra-service-01, infra-ci-02, infra-ops], common_change_id=chg_2026-03-12-0918
Sam R.: Can we avoid relying on low-severity tags for auth-sensitive alerts? Prefer whitelisting by `change_id` from the change-control system instead.
Irina K.: Yes — let's wire change-control -> SIEM so every role-change includes `change_id` and `initiator`. Playbook item: require `change_id` param in the RBAC automation.
Jonah M.: Short-term: I'm going to push a temporary rule patch to collapse repeats and add a suppression for known `change_id` values. Long-term: integrate the deployment system with SIEM.
Carmen L.: I'll update the RBAC runbook to include a post-change audit query and a tag pattern. Also note to notify on-call sec before bulk role updates.
Sam R.: For the KMS decrypt failures — can infra reapply grants to the service accounts? Might be a timing gap where roles removed before key policies were updated.
Carmen L.: Looks like keypolicy change is separate. I'm opening a quick change to rebind kms-access role to the affected SAs.
Irina K.: Who's owning post-incident? We need a short incident note and a follow-up checklist: 1) revert temporary SIEM rule, 2) persist rule tuning (grouping), 3) integrate change_id producer, 4) update RBAC runbook, 5) add dashboard widget for RBAC-change spikes.
Jonah M.: I'll own the SIEM rule patch and dashboard widget. Sam — can you handle the KMS binding fix? Carmen — update runbook and postmortem.
Sam R.: On it. KMS fix pushed (eta 12m).
sec-bot: KMS bindings adjusted for principals: infra-service-01, infra-ci-02, infra-ops. Status: success.
Jonah M.: SIEM grouping live and suppression expired; alert volume dropped to baseline. Thanks.
Irina K.: Nice work. Action items: Carmen to file post-incident report with timeline and suggested guardrails (change_id enforcement). Jonah to commit grouped rule to policy-as-code. Sam to validate KMS replay/rollout sequence. I'll schedule a 30-min retro. :white_check_mark:
Carmen L.: Filing the post-incident doc now. Will link after it's up.
Jonah M.: PR incoming for the grouped rule and dashboard (refs: #4232).
Sam R.: Running a replay test of role-update -> kms-access flow; will post results.
Irina K.: Closing thread once postmortem live. Thanks everyone. :heart:
